## Proof

We determine $k(\alpha) \otimes_k L$ up to isomorphism.

**Claim.** $k(\alpha) \otimes_k L \cong L[x]/(f(x))$, where $f(x)$ is regarded as a polynomial in $L[x]$ via the canonical embedding $k \hookrightarrow L$.

**Proof.** Since $f \in k[x]$ is irreducible and $\alpha$ is a root of $f$, the evaluation map
$$\mathrm{ev}_\alpha : k[x] \to k(\alpha), \quad g(x) \mapsto g(\alpha)$$
is a surjective $k$-algebra homomorphism with kernel $(f(x))$. Hence, by the first isomorphism theorem,
$$k(\alpha) \cong k[x]/(f(x)) \tag{1}$$
as $k$-algebras.

Tensor product is a functor, so applying $-\otimes_k L$ to (1) gives a canonical isomorphism of $L$-algebras:
$$k(\alpha) \otimes_k L \;\cong\; \big(k[x]/(f(x))\big) \otimes_k L. \tag{2}$$

We now simplify the right-hand side. There is a general isomorphism for any ideal $I \subseteq k[x]$:
$$\big(k[x]/I\big) \otimes_k L \;\cong\; L[x]/(I\cdot L[x]), \tag{3}$$
where $I \cdot L[x]$ is the ideal generated by $I$ in $L[x]$.

To verify (3) explicitly: consider the $k$-bilinear (in fact $L$-balanced) map
$$\varphi : k[x] \times L \to L[x]/(I\cdot L[x]), \quad (g(x),\, \ell) \mapsto \overline{\ell \cdot g(x)}.$$
This is $k$-balanced, so it descends to a $k$-linear (indeed $L$-linear) map
$$\widetilde\varphi : k[x] \otimes_k L \to L[x]/(I\cdot L[x]).$$
Since every element of $L[x]$ is a finite sum $\sum \ell_i x^i = \sum x^i \otimes \ell_i$, the map $\widetilde\varphi$ is surjective. Its kernel is $I \otimes_k L = I \cdot L[x]$ (viewed inside $k[x]\otimes_k L \cong L[x]$), so by the first isomorphism theorem,
$$\big(k[x]/I\big)\otimes_k L \cong L[x]/(I\cdot L[x]).$$

Applying (3) with $I = (f(x))$, we have $I \cdot L[x] = (f(x))$ in $L[x]$ (the ideal generated by $f$, now viewed in $L[x]$). Therefore
$$k(\alpha) \otimes_k L \;\cong\; L[x]/(f(x)). \tag{4}$$

**Consequences / structure.** The structure of $L[x]/(f(x))$ depends on how $f$ factors over $L$:

- If $f$ remains irreducible over $L$, then $L[x]/(f(x))$ is a field, so $k(\alpha)\otimes_k L$ is a field.
- If $f$ factors over $L$ as $f = f_1^{e_1}\cdots f_r^{e_r}$ with $f_i$ distinct irreducibles in $L[x]$, then by the Chinese Remainder Theorem (applied to the pairwise coprime factors $f_i^{e_i}$),
$$L[x]/(f(x)) \cong \prod_{i=1}^{r} L[x]/(f_i(x)^{e_i}).$$
In particular, if $f$ is separable over $L$ (all $e_i = 1$), this is a product of fields, each isomorphic to $L(\beta_i)$ for a root $\beta_i$ of $f$ in some extension of $L$.

In all cases, the canonical isomorphism is
$$\boxed{\,k(\alpha)\otimes_k L \;\cong\; L[x]/(f(x))\,}$$
as $L$-algebras, with the isomorphism sending $\alpha \otimes 1 \mapsto \bar{x}$ (the class of $x$ in $L[x]/(f(x))$) and $1 \otimes \ell \mapsto \bar\ell$.

### PROOF COMPLETE
